title: Regional Stewardship Binding and Compliance Dossier Automation for Hosted Endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers operating under data residency requirements need a reliable way to lock hosted API traffic to a specific jurisdiction, set retention policies at the endpoint level, and produce tamper-evident compliance bundles for audits. Current hosted endpoints accept region preferences but lack: (1) operator-friendly binding semantics (hard vs. advisory pin), (2) per-endpoint retention configuration surfaced in Console/APIs, and (3) an automated evidence "dossier" builder that packages routing decisions, access logs, retention proofs, and attestations for auditors.

Proposal: Build a Regional Stewardship Binding feature that supports both hard binding (strict regional enforcement) and stewardship (preferred-region with fallback policies). Pair bindings with per-endpoint retention controls, and add a Compliance Dossier Automation pipeline that generates signed, time-stamped bundles containing routing traces, storage retention headers, customer configuration snapshots, and a compact evidence index for export. The dossier will be downloadable from Console and obtainable via a dedicated API endpoint for enterprise customers.

Scope (this ticket):
- Define binding semantics and API surface for region binding (hard, soft, stewarded) and retention TTL per hosted endpoint.
- Implement backend policy checks + routing enforcement flags and a fallback policy engine for soft bindings.
- Design Console UX for binding creation/editing and retention controls with clear compliance language.
- Implement a Compliance Dossier builder that aggregates relevant artifacts on-demand and on-schedule (daily/weekly), signs bundles with KMS, and stores them in the customer’s evidence bucket or returns them via API.
- Add telemetry and dashboards for binding effectiveness, failures, and dossier generation success rates.

Out of scope:
- On-prem/private deployment adaptations (tracked under PM-xxx-private-adapt).
- Long-term retention archive integrations beyond S3-compatible targets.

Success criteria: End-to-end flow where an enterprise tenant can pin an endpoint to EU-West-1 as a hard binding, have retained request/response metadata for 90 days per retention config, and produce a cryptographically-signed compliance dossier within 30 minutes of request that contains the artifacts listed in acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: API: Create/Update endpoint binding API accepts {type: "hard|soft|steward", region: string, fallback_policy: optional} and returns 200 with validation errors for unsupported regions.
Console: Binding editor shows clear language about enforcement, fallback cost/latency trade-offs, and a retention TTL control tied to the endpoint.
Routing: Hard bindings cause non-compliant requests to be rejected or quarantined with explicit error code; soft bindings route preferring pinned region and record fallback events in trace logs.
Dossier: On-demand dossier API returns a signed ZIP containing (routing-trace.jsonl, retention-policy-snapshot.json, access-log.snappy, evidence-index.toml) and a KMS signature metadata file.
Observability: New dashboards surface binding violations per tenant, average fallback latency, dossier generation latency, and dossier generation failure rate (<2%).
Security: Evidence bundles are encrypted at rest and signatures are validated by our QA process before GA.
comments: 2025-11-13 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff notes added. Initial stakeholder list includes Security, Runtime, Console, and BD. Requested a feasibility spike with Infra and ENG to evaluate KMS signing and storage options.

2025-12-01 - Luca Martinez: Feasibility spike results: KMS signing OK, storage approach needs per-tenant evidence buckets; ENG estimates +5 points for adding per-tenant storage plumbing. Raising estimate from 5 -> 8.

2026-01-07 - Priya Shah (Security): Reviewed proposed dossier contents. Asked to add tamper-evidence timeline (hash chain) and to require signed manifest for each bundle. Marked security_review_required = true.
2026-01-22 - Design review (Ava Kim): Console mockups iterate to clarify 'hard' vs 'soft' wording and added an inline simulator showing expected routing behavior for pinned regions.

2026-02-10 - Eng update (Marco Rossi): Implemented routing enforcement flags. Early QA shows soft binding fallbacks are logged but rare edge-case where region capacity 0 caused silent failover — adding explicit quarantine path. Filed ENG-11890.
2026-02-28 - PM review (Luca Martinez): Updated acceptance criteria to require dossier generation latency <= 30 minutes for on-demand requests and <2% failure rate for scheduled bundles.
2026-03-05 - Security (Priya Shah): Completed review staging notes. Need KMS rotation handling documented; flagged for additional testing during canary.
2026-03-09 - Release (Jordan Lee): Suggested rollout gating: GA only after successful 2-week canary on 3 tenants and tabletop audit walkthrough. Added to release checklist.
decision_records: 2025-12-05: Chosen KMS-based signature + per-tenant evidence buckets vs centralized evidence store to minimize cross-tenant leakage risk.

2026-01-10: Binding types defined as 'hard' (reject non-local), 'soft' (prefer local, record fallback), 'steward' (prefer local but allow multi-region routing for critical customer performance—requires explicit SLA).
2026-02-12: Dossier format chosen as compressed tarball with JSONL traces and a TOML index for easy parsing by auditors and automation tools.
migration_steps: Add binding metadata column to endpoint config table and backfill existing endpoints with 'soft' default.
Deploy routing enforcement toggle behind runtime feature flag for canary tenants.
Run two-week canary: enable on 3 consenting enterprise tenants, monitor binding violations and dossier generation metrics.
Rollout to remaining tenants in phased batches with automated rollback on quota/failure thresholds.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Launch internal alpha for Compliance & Solutions engineering to exercise dossier retrieval and validate manifests.
Week 1-2: Two-week external canary with 3 tenants, gated by dossier success metrics and binding violation thresholds.
Week 3-5: Gradual ramp to 25% of enterprise tenants; collect feedback and remediate UX wording issues.
Week 6: GA with public docs, SDK updates, and a migration playbook for enterprise customers.
metrics: binding_enforcement_rate: percent of requests that conformed to hard bindings vs blocked
fallback_rate: percent of requests that fell back from pinned region
dossier_latency_ms: 95p latency for on-demand dossier generation
dossier_failure_rate: percent of scheduled or on-demand dossier requests that failed
